title: Insects and mites in the fauna of Serbia - importance for the classical biological control of weeds
venue: AgroSpace (University of Belgrade, Faculty of Agriculture)
abstract: Territory of the Republic of Serbia, as the central area of the Balkan Peninsula, is of particular interest as a point where biological entities coming from central Europe, Asia Minor, Mediterranean and North Africa encounter. Hence, this area has been declared as a "center of European biodiversity". Natural consequence of Serbia's geographic position and the richness of the flora is the great diversity of insect fauna (Insecta). Observed diversity of entomofauna is the reason why the territory of Serbia is attractive for the research in biological control. Climate change and the intensive exchange of biota as a direct consequence of increasing global trend of trade between the countries is what make this a particularly important issue. Although Serbia has a relatively short history of research on phytophagous insects as biological control agents for Eurasian origin weeds, researchers at the biological laboratory of Institute for plant protection based in Zemun (presently Institute for plant protection and environment, Zemun) can be considered as doyens of biological control research in Europe and even worldwide. The first department for biological control of pests in Europe started working in the Institute for plant protection in Zemun, in 1954. The founder and the first director of the Institute for plant protection, prof. dr. Guido Nonveiller, had a vision of forming a team of interdisciplinary researchers with biological and agronomic BACKGROUND: . In the period from 1967-1974, the project entitled "Project 480: Europe: Yugoslavia E30-Ent-12 - Distribution and natural enemies of the weeds Dalmatian toadflax (Linaria dalmatica Mill) and Mediterranean sage (Salvia aethiopsis L.) in Yugoslavia", has been carried out for the purpose of biological control of L. dalmatica (Plantaginaceae) and Salvia aethiops (Lamiaceae). Four more projects supported by the USDA followed: Elaboration of protective measures for agricultural crops against parasitic phanerogams belonging to the genera Cuscuta and Orobanche (parasitic herbs - dodders and broomrape) (1968-1971), Biological control of terrestrial and aquatic weeds and pests of crop plants (1977-1983), Biological control of insects and weeds (1981-1986), Biocontrol of Yugoslavian and North American weeds with insects, pathogens and other biotic agents (1988-1990, 1991). Research on potential phytophagous insects against invasive weeds in North America included, beside a forementioned plants, Myriophyllum spicatum L. (Haloragaceae), Carduus nutans, Carduus acanthoides, Cirsium arvense, Centaurea solstitialis, Centaurea maculosa (Asteraceae), Euphorbia cyparissias and Euphorbia virgata (Euphorbaceae). Classical biological control (i.e. intentional release of natural enemies of exotic pests for the purpose of their control) represents a very important tool in the integrated pest management. Globalization and intensive trade between countries have led to exchange of organisms from different zoogeographical regions. Should those organisms adapt to the new environment, they could potentially represent threat to local ecosystems. This is the reason why, according to Agenda 21 (Chapter 14), biological control has been recognized as a method of choice in pest control. Until 1992, the research within USDA Project 480 resulted in introduction of several insect species in the area of North America. Introduced species were: Sphenoptera jugoslavica for the purpose of controlling Centaurea diffusa (Asteraceae), Hylas euphorbiae, Oberea erythrocephala, Pegomya euphorbiae and P. curticornis (Diptera: Anthomyiidae) for the control of invasive spurge species Euphorbia esula, E. cyparissias and E. virgata. Species from the genus Aphthona (Coleoptera, Chrysomelidae), A. lacertosa, A. nigris-cutis and A. flava, were introduced for the same reason. Further, two weevil species, Larinus obtusus and L. minutus (Coleoptera, Curculionidae), were used against Centaurea diffusa and Centaurea maculosa. Lastly, defoliator species Calophasia lunula (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) was introduced for the control of Linaria dalmatica and L. vulgaris (Plantaginaceae). During the period of 1992-1999, introduced species were Chamaesphecia hungarica and Ch. crassicornis for the control of Euphorbia virgata and Chamaesphecia hungarica for the control of Euphorbia esula. Two moth species, Eteobalea serratella and E. intermediella (Cosmopterigidae), were introduced for the control of north American populations of Linaria vulgaris and L. dalmatica. Finally, after extensive host specificity tests, a weevil species Mogulones cruciger was introduced for the purpose of controlling Cynoglossum officinale (Boraginaceae) in North America. Advances in molecular techniques in the 21st century have led to turn over in biological control research. New knowledge on specific interactions within the insect-plant system has placed in the focus population-genetic properties of the biological control agent. Molecular techniques also enabled understanding biological properties of local insect's populations as well as cryptic speciation, which consequently led to overall better safety and precision in biological control research. The research, since 2000, has been focused on invasive plant species of the genus Linaria and weevils of the genus Mecinus and Rhinusa. New research enabled introduction and successful development of gallicol weevil species Rhinusapilosa in north-west Canada. Furthermore, cryptic species Mecinus janthiniformis was described within the Mecinus jathinus. Within Mecinus heydenii complex of species, one cryptic species were described, Mecinus peterharrisi in association with L. dalmatica and one subspecies Mecinus laeviceps ssp. meridionalis association with L. genistifolia from East Serbia and Bulgaria. One new gallforming weevil species was also described, namely Rhinusa rara in association with L. genistifolia and L. dalmatica from East Serbia, Hungary and South Russia. All newly described species and subspecies are in the research process of suitability assessment as the biological control agents. Besides insects many species of eriophyoid mites, an obligatory plant feeders, are considered to be among the most promising candidate agents for classical biological control of weeds due to their biology and host-plant relationship. Eriophyoid mites have high degree of host specificity, about 80% of currently known species have been recorded on a one host plant. Among approximately 5000 known species about 50 are considered as potential weed control agents in the world. More than 50% of these species have been discovered in Serbia. Investigations in this field started in early 1980's. In the period 1990-2000's in the framework of different projects three new species for science were described on Geranium dissectum L. and four on Euphorbia spp. At the beginning of 2000's, especially detailed studies of Aceria anthocoptes (Nal.) and Leipothrix dipsacivagus Petanovic. et Rector have been carried out from the different points of view. During the last years few eriophyoid mites were investigated within the framework of different European programs of classical biological control of weeds. Aceria acroptiloni Kovalev et Shevchenko was studied as agent of biocontrol of Rhaponticum repens (L.) Hidalgo, Metaculus spp. were studied for biological control of Lepidium latifolium L., Isatis tinctoria and Diplotaxis tenuifolia, as well as two Aceria spp. for biological control of Eleagnus angustifolia L. Moreover two potential biocontrol agents Aceria artemisiifoliae Vidovic & Petanovic, and Aculops mosiniensis Ripka against Ambrosia artemisifolia L. and Ailanthus altissima (Mill) Swingle respectively have been nominated recently. More or less integrative approach in species delimitation has been applied using combined techniques of phase contrast light microscopy, pseudo dark field, differential interference contrast microscopy, confocal laser scanning microscopy, scanning electron microscopy and sequencing of barcoding region of mt COI DNA. Traditional morphological analysis was accomplished with morphometric, (linear and/or geometric) analysis because it helps in understanding intraspecific variability, including races adapted to the host plants and /or cryptic species. Studying potential agents for the biological control of invasive weeds is tightly linked with floristic and entomo-acaro-faunistic diversity. Because of its position, the territory of Serbia represents a meeting point for floristic and faunistic elements coming from central Europe, Asia Minor, Mediterranean and North Africa. The complex floristic and faunistic diversity is also a consequence of numerous colonizations and recolonizations of biota during the periods of glaciation and interglaciation. These unique aspects have made the territory of Serbia an excellent starting point for the research in biological control.

title: MANUFACTURERS NEWS
abstract: Grason-Stadler unveils new data-management software EDEN PRAIRIE, MN—Grason-Stadler (GSI) has introduced GSI Suite, its new audiometric data-management software. This is an important milestone for GSI since it now provides EMR compatibility on its flagship product. GSI Suite captures, saves, and shares patient information and improves reporting to support the needs of the contemporary clinic. The new system's features include: test results in an EMR-compatible format (PDF), the ability to retrieve test results for review, printing reports from PC-compliant printers, ability to e-mail PDF reports, and the networking of results by combining GSI Suite with OtoAccess™.FigureGSI Suite currently provides EMR compatibility with the GSI 61, and will be available on additional products in the coming months. GSI Suite is now included with all new GSI 61 orders. Further information on GSI Suite is available from GSI at: 800/700-2282 (U.S.) or 952/278-4402 (international), or by visiting www.grason-stadler.com or e-mailing [email protected]. Oticon Safari adds Super Power for kids SOMERSET, NJ—Safari Super Power (SP) is the newest member of Oticon's Safari family of hearing solutions for children. It comes equipped with high-quality components to deliver reliability and provide both the audibility and higher signal fidelity needed to preserve the speech signal in the natural, undistorted form that children with severe-to-profound hearing loss require.Figure“Children with severe-profound hearing loss need access to as many sounds as possible,” said George Lindley, PhD, AuD, manager of Oticon Pediatrics ([email protected]). “The negative consequences of traditional compression on important speech cues can limit a child's ability to function in dynamic sound environments such as the classroom, sports field or playground.” Changes at Unitron announced STAFA, SWITZERLAND—Sonova Holding AG (www.sonova.com), has announced that Cameron Hay stood down as president and CEO of Unitron (www.unitron.com), a division of Sonova, on November 30 after over 5 years as a member of the Sonova management board. The announcement said that Hay left “to take on new professional and personal challenges outside the group.” Sonova plans to appoint a successor shortly. Appointments at Unitron US Meanwhile, Unitron has appointed Chue Yang as senior operations manager and Brian Taylor, AuD, as director of practice development and clinical affairs, both at Unitron US. In his new position, Yang oversees manufacturing operations. Rodney Schutt, president and CEO of the company, said that in his 16 years at Unitron US, Yang has been “a leading force behind many improvements in our manufacturing processes and product quality.” He began in 1994 as an operator in manufacturing and was promoted to lead technician then manufacturing manager in 2002.Figure: Chue YangFigure: Brian TaylorTaylor, who heads the Unite customer loyalty program launched last July, also directs Unitron's best practices and clinical research initiatives and is responsible for all company initiatives related to key opinions, leadership, and clinical best practices. He was previously manager of professional services at Unitron, which he joined after holding various positions with Amplifon. He also has about 15 years of experience managing practices and fitting hearing aids. He holds his AuD from Central Michigan University. Researchers praise Oticon Medical processor COPENHAGEN—Preliminary results of the first independent study of differences in two new bone-conduction sound processors indicate that Oticon Medical's Ponto Pro sound processor is superior to the other major brand of processor on the market. The study, conducted by researchers at Rigshospitalet in Copenhagen, involved individuals with conductive and mixed hearing loss who were first-time users of bone-anchored hearing systems.FigureResearchers presented their preliminary findings at two recent international conferences in Stockholm and Vejle, Denmark. Twelve subjects with conductive and mixed hearing loss tested each device for an average of 34 days in their daily environments. Subjects rated the sound processors at the end of each test period. The study found statistically significant superiority for Ponto Pro for speech perception and ease of use. Oticon Medical (www.oticomedical.com) recently made four additions to the Ponto system of advanced sound processors, accessories, implant components, and surgical instruments. They reflect the company's emphasis on user-focused innovation in surgical treatment and audiological solutions for people with conductive/mixed hearing losses and single-sided deafness. “The refinements in the surgical components represent collaboration between Oticon Medical and leading university and medical center clinics to enhance the quality and further the development of the treatment of conductive hearing,” said Jes Olsen, CEO of Oticon Medical. Sona convenes advisory council CHICAGO—Sona Hearing, LLC, a new company of Sonova, has formed Sona: Hearing Professional Advisory Council to understand how to better help patients with hearing loss and the hearing care professionals who serve them. Sona Hearing reached out to 13 experts in hearing care from across the United States to advise the company on the current unmet needs in the hearing aid marketplace. The company wanted to gain insights from the hearing professionals through the open dialogue of an advisory council forum. Advising Sona Hearing were: Tricia Ashby, AuD, Towson University, MD; Bopanna Ballachanda, PhD, Premier Hearing Centers, Santa Fe, NM; William W. Dickinson, AuD, Vanderbilt University; Denny P. Dingler II, BC-HIS, Professional Hearing Centers, Inverness, FL; Timothy C Dunnigan, AuD, Advanced Hearing Technology, Naples, FL; Donald Hawley, MS, BC-HIS, Sound Advice Hearing Solutions, St. Petersburg, FL; Victoria A. Hingst, AuD, Advanced Hearing Technology, Naples, FL; Gail Linn, AuD, Potomac Audiology, Rockville, MD; Paul Pessis, AuD, North Shore Audio-Vestibular Lab, Highland Park, IL; David E. Rich, PhD, Binson's Hearing Aid Services, Clarkston, MI; Sharon A. Sandridge, PhD, The Cleveland (OH) Clinic; Diane Schrager, private practice, Arlington Heights, IL; and Gregory D. Wales, BC-HIS, Wales Hearing Center, Alexandria, MN. Further information is available from Barry Hylas at: 630/821-9704 or at www.sonapro.com. Hansaton unveils Speech Beam MINNEAPOLIS—Hansaton USA (www.hansaton-usa.com) has begun offering hearing aids with its new Speech Beam directional processing technology. Speech Beam locates the primary speech source from the front, side, or behind and enhances the preferred signal accordingly. The result, says the company, is improved speech intelligibility from all directions. “Most designs find the primary noise source and then try to cancel it out. In contrast, Speech Beam finds the primary speech source and then steers the maximum response angle (MRA) to enhance that speech,” said Jerry Yanz, director of audiology for Hansaton. According to the company, Speech Beam benefits include eliminating the problem hearing aid users often encounter when driving a car or participating in any activity that requires recognizing speech from people behind or beside them. Speech Beam is offered in Auriga BTEs, Auriga directional ITEs, and the AQ Custom Rechargeable Hearing Systems. AHAA plans 2011 Convention LAS VEGAS—American Hearing Aid Associates (AHAA) will hold its 15th annual convention here at the Palazzo Resort Hotel February 16–19. More than 400 hearing healthcare professionals—associates in the AHAA network and others—are expected to attend. “Each year our convention seems to re-energize our associates,” said Tina Soika, AHAA president. “Our goal this time is to direct their motivation toward improving all aspects of their practices, especially their growth.” This focus inspired the convention's theme, “Your Success, Realized.” The convention will offer nearly 40 ASHA, AAA, and IHS-approved sessions, with CEUs granted, covering all aspects of running a practice. Also planned are roundtable networking sessions for peer-to-peer discussions and manufacturer exhibits and workshops to discuss the latest changes and trends in technology and products. More information is available from Ashley Fox at 800/984-3272 or at [email protected]. HearUSA reaches out to vets WEST PALM BEACH, FL—HearUSA, Inc. (www.hearusa.com), commemorated Veterans Day by raising awareness of its year-long partnership with Veterans Care Plus, a health advocacy group, to offer affordable hearing care to the millions of veterans and their family members who do not qualify for benefits through the VA. “HearUSA wants to honor the contribution of our fine servicemen and women, as well as the sacrifices made by their family members,” said Steve Hansbrough, chairman and CEO. The program focuses on educating veterans and their families about hearing loss and the importance of good hearing care. It offers personalized evaluations and hearing care options. Benefits include access to more than 2000 licensed hearing care providers nationwide, savings on a wide range of digital hearing aids, extended warranties, and interest-free financing. Record throng at Audigy event VANCOUVER, WA—Audigy Group (www.audigygroup.com) drew a record number of attendees to its November Patients for Life™ training summit held in November in Baltimore. Nearly 200 Audigy Group members and their staff from over 51 practices nationwide, along with 25 Audigy Group staff, took part in the 2-day educational conference.Figure: Terrance Ford, Don Szmanda and Jeff Koch were among the throng in Dallas.The meeting was the first to merge Audigy's duplicable patient interaction program designed to maximize patient retention and satisfaction with its digital counterpart, e-patient™, a visual education platform for the exam room, into its curriculum. New from Bellman & Symfon GOTHENBURG, SWEDEN—Bellman & Symfon (www.bellman.se/us/audio) has introduced Mino™, a fully digital personal amplifier for the consumer market with both omni- and directional microphone technology. Mino's features include high-definition audio technology (HDA), zoom function, and the latest cell phone battery technology. The device, which is thin and light enough to fit discreetly in the pocket, can provide up to 18 hours of continuous amplified speech and music on a single battery charge.FigureAvada meeting is a big draw DALLAS—Nearly 200 hearing clinicians attended the Avada Business Conference here last fall. The conference was held to advance practitioners' ability and skills and provide them with the latest best practice applications so they can better help their patients. The theme, “The Power of One,” was selected to illustrate the power of one company, with one protocol and one mission, to serve the hearing impaired with the highest degree of professionalism, technology, and service available. The keynote speaker was Karin Iwata, of E-Myth Worldwide. Iwata spoke on the importance of standardizing procedures and protocols, which Avada (www.avada.com) has implemented nationwide. FDA okays Med-El processor DURHAM, NC—Med-El Corporation USA (www.medel.com) has received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for the Amadé™ audio processor for use with the Vibrant Soundbridge® middle ear implant system, which is designed for people with moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss. The Amadé distinguishes between speech and background noise and helps the user communicate in a wide range of situations. It features multiple programs, wind noise reduction, sound smoothing, and speech and noise management. BlackBerry app introduced COLORADO SPRINGS, CO—During the ALDAcon 2010 Conference,. Hamilton CapTel (www.HamiltonCapTel.com) announced a new application for BlackBerry® smart phones designed to enable people with hearing loss to communicate effectively with captioned telephone services on BlackBerry smart phones. With the Hamilton Mobile CapTel App, consumers can see what they say directly on their BlackBerry smart phone. Like closed captioning on TV, captioned telephone service allows users to talk on their phone and listen and read captions of their conversation on the screen on their BlackBerry device. Beltone, Starkey win consumer honors LAS VEGAS—Beltone Electronics and Starkey Laboratories, Inc., will both receive the prestigious International CES Innovations 2011 Design and Engineering Award for new products. The International CES, which is sponsored, produced, and managed by the Consumer Electronics Association, is the world's largest consumer electronics tradeshow. The 2011 International CES will be held here January 6–9. Chicago-based Beltone (www.beltone.com) was honored for Beltone True™, a new generation of virtually invisible Bluetooth-compatible hearing instruments that wirelessly receive sound directly from TV, cell/home phone, stereo, PC, and iPod via a 2.4-GHz signal. It allows users to comfortably converse with those nearby while listening to music or watching their favorite TV program. Minneapolis-based Starkey (www.starkey.com) won its award for OtoLens™, the first custom invisible-in-the-canal hearing aid. This is the third consecutive year Starkey has been an honoree, having won for the S Series™ with Sweep™ Technology and Zon™ previously.
